(Yogendra Sangle Vs The State Of Madhya Prade
 Dated : 16-02-2024
Shri Rameshwar Rawat - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Dinesh Savita - Public Prosecutor for respondent/St
Heard on the question of admission.
The appeal being arguable is admitted for final hearing.
Heard on I.A.No.16843 of 2023, first application under Section 389 (1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

The appeal has been preferred by the appellant under Section 374 of Cr.P.C. against the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence dated 23.08.2023 passed by First Additional Sessions Judge ,Datia (M.P.) in ST No.101/2018 whereby appellant has been convicted and sentenced under Section 376 of IPC to undergo rigorous imprisonment of ten years with fine of Rs.2000/-, with default stipulation.
Learned counsel for the appellant argued that learned trial court has wrongly convicted the appellant without considering the evidence available on record.
Further submission is that on the basis of evidence adduced by prosecution as well as statement of PW-5 (prosecutrix), it is evident that at the time of incident, her age was 30 years.
She was a married major woman.
From perusal of her cross-examination at paras 13, 14, 15, 40, it is apparent that this is a matter of consent and consensual sexual relationship.

Further submission is that the entire prosecution story is highly improbable because next day, the prosecutrix has admitted that in next day, she visited temple and she did not inform the hotel staff or anyone or other person about the alleged sexual assault by the appellant.
Further submission is that appellant has already suffered 14 months' incarceration out of total jail sentence.

This criminal appeal is likely to take long time to come up for final hearing and appellant has hope and believe that he would succeed, therefore, prayed to suspend the jail sentence of the appellant.
On the other hand, learned Public Prosecutor for respondent /State opposed the application and prayed for rejection of the same.

sentences.text:
Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, without commenting on merits of the case, it is directed that subject to depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited,
and on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail.
He is further directed to mark his presence before the Registry of this Court on 28.5.2024 and on subsequent dates as may be given in this regard till final disposal of this appeal.
List the case for final hearing in due course.
A copy of this order be sent to the concerned Court below for compliance.
Certified copy/ e-copy as per rules/directions.

(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE AK/-
